investors: FTX Future Fund (offered; rejected by board)

target_customer: General public, journalists, researchers and policymakers (free); funded by donors and grants
problem: Reliable long-run data on global problems is scattered and hard to understand.
business_model: nonprofit funded by philanthropic grants and reader donations

founders.name: Max Roser
founders.background_notes: Social historian and development economist; began the project 2011, launched May 2013 (Wikipedia).

founders.name: Hannah Ritchie
founders.background_notes: Joined 2017, later Head of Research per Wikipedia; YC lists her as founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Data aggregation and interactive charts; open-source tooling.

defensibility.rationale: Curated datasets, trust and reputation built over a decade; content freely reusable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent attempted to absorb it in sources seen; not exhaustively researched.

market_need_then: Not researched with dated sources; the stated need is accessible, reliable long-run data on global problems such as poverty, disease and climate.

branding.community_and_virality: Won the 2019 Lovie Award; widely used in media (Wikipedia notes award; media use not examined).

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized, award-winning web brand cited widely, per Wikipedia; breadth of media use not independently checked.

outcome_analysis: Our World in Data is a nonprofit that joined YC Winter 2019 as one of three nonprofits, so venture outcome metrics do not apply. It has been sustained by grants and over 4,000 donors by 2023, with 2023 revenue of GBP 2.45M per Wikipedia and staff growth from 6 to about 20; success here means durable funding and reach, not an exit.
notes: The web search budget was exhausted before the required outcome, funding cross-check, dated-competitor and branding searches could run, so competition_at_founding is empty and brand fields rest only on the YC page and the company site. The 2022 FTX Future Fund USD 7.5M was an offer the board rejected, so it is not a received round; recorded only to show the grant, with the rejection stated here (the schema has no field for this). Nonprofit, not a normal venture comp: founded 2013 before the 2019 YC batch. Funding single-source (Wikipedia).
